listing.voiceover: Uma moradia com terraço e dois lugares de estacionamento. Na Calçada do Pico, em São Pedro, a minutos do centro do Funchal. Dois pisos: sala e cozinha equipada em baixo, dois quartos em cima. Lá fora, terraço, varanda e logradouro. Trezentos e sessenta mil euros. Para visitar, fale com o Gonçalo Luís, da REMAX.

anim.prompt: Furnish the outdoor entrance patio with modern furniture, including a long slatted light-oak bench with soft off-white cushions, large matte terracotta and charcoal planters filled with olive trees, ferns and grasses, a low outdoor rug and a modern black wall light. Add a flowering arch of pink bougainvillea and white jasmine above the bench, framing the hexagonal screen without covering any of its openings, plus lush greenery in the existing low planter at the bottom right. Paint the walls a warm soft white. Replace the outdoor floor with large-format warm light-beige stone-look porcelain tiles. Place the bench along the low wall directly beneath the hexagonal screen, with the planters grouped at the right corner. Keep the staircase on the left with its steps, the dark doorway at the top of the stairs on the left and the white hexagonal breeze-block screen in the centre-right wall clear and exactly as they are. Make everything proportional to the space. All the furniture should be modern and cozy in style.
keep: the open doorway to a corridor on the left edge, near wall
the staircase on the left, near wall
the decorative partition in the centre, back wall
problems: Decorative partition resized and redesigned: it is narrower and shorter (about 42–80% of frame width, top edge lowered), with noticeably larger and fewer hexagon cells than the real block screen
Partition's lower rows replaced: a built-in bench with a slatted base cuts into the bottom of the screen, so the lower hexagon courses that sit above the white panel in the real photo are gone
clip_problems: Frames 2–3: a window with frames appears at the top right, on the right-hand wall. It is not in the first frame or the final still. It is gone again by frame 4.
Frames 1→2: the right-hand wall changes from rough grey textured render into a smooth beige wall with a ledge and a window. This is structural morphing, not just a new finish.

Frames 1→2: the left-hand wall morphs. The long peeling side wall running down the corridor shrinks and turns into a short wall fragment, and a wall with a doorway and staircase grows out of the space behind it. The room's geometry is being reshaped.
Frames 1→2: the corridor's open continuation behind and above the partition (the dark gap at the back in the first frame and frame 1) closes up into a solid beige back wall.

Frame 1→2: there are two hexagonal lattice panels in frame 1 (the front partition and a second recessed panel on the right). The second panel disappears or merges into one, so a lattice opening vanishes.
Frame 2: the decorative partition warps badly. The left half of the hexagon lattice is smeared and melted into distorted blobs, and its frame moves and changes shape between frames 1, 2 and 3.

Frames 1→2: the doorway to the corridor and the staircase on the left appear out of nowhere where frame 1 shows a solid peeling wall. Openings that should stay fixed are coming into existence mid-video instead of staying consistent.

problems: Camera framing is very different from the real photo: the view is pulled far back and the room is re-composed into a wide living-room shot.
The centre French doors are resized. They are much narrower than in the real photo and no longer fill the central part of the back wall.
The sofa is pushed against the bottom of the floor-length centre French doors and blocks them.
The closed wooden built-in wardrobe on the right has been partly turned into open shelving with plants and objects, so it is no longer an all-closed wardrobe of the same size.
clip_problems: Frame 2: the built-in wardrobe on the back wall changes shape. Its two equal sliding doors become one wide door plus a narrow, dark, recessed strip on the right, as if a door has slid partly open or the unit has warped.

Frame 3: the wardrobe morphs. Its top cornice bends and curves, and the front of the unit angles out from the back wall instead of staying flat against it as it does in the first frame and the final still.

Frames 2–4: the centre window/door on the back wall shifts relative to the room. The wall between it and the left corner widens steadily, more than the camera movement explains, so the opening appears to slide towards the centre of the wall.
